newsitem.title: UK: GDR REPORT - Thin trade sees India marked lower.
newsitem.headline: GDR REPORT - Thin trade sees India marked lower.

text.p: Thin trade in Indian global depositary receipts (GDRs) saw the market marked lower after a slow day in Bombay.
"The market is slightly weaker, not much is happening. There are no client buyers, no direction from the local market," said a trader.
The HSBC James Capel Indian GDR index JCEAI closed down 0.54 points, 0.80 percent, at 66.26 points, with the premium over the local market at 12.33 percent compared with yesterday's 12.89 percent.
The Bombay Stock Exchange 30-share index fell 6.75 points to 3,382.74.

The Capel Korea GDR Index ended off 1.61 points, 2.29 percent, at 68.69, a premium of 49.41 percent over the local market, after the Korea Composite Index fell 27.92 points, or 3.89 percent, to provisionally close at 690.54.
"Korean GDRs remain thinly traded, premiums are firm," said a trader.
The Capel Taiwan GDR Index ended up 0.41 points at 99.43, a premium of 7.38 percent after the Taiwan Weighted Index fell 3.26 points to 7,251.04.
